channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Gathered VII: Georgia Artists Selecting Georgia Artists · Museum of Contemporary Art of Georgia
item.description: The seventh instalment of MOCA GA's biennial exhibition built on a single idea: Georgia artists choose Georgia artists. The museum describes the project as the one in which “the MOCA GA mission is fully realized … as artists are involved in all phases of the exhibition, including selection and review”, and the series has run since 2006 under three successive names — Within State Lines (2006, 2009), Georgia Artists Selecting Georgia Artists (2013, 2015) and, since then, Gathered. This round is the first to be staged in MOCA GA's new building by Mack Scogin Merrill Elam Architects. The jury is three Georgia artists named on the call, each with a bio on the museum's own jurors page: Hannah Israel, gallery director and professor of art at Columbus State University; Craig Drennen, a painter and 2018 Guggenheim fellow who teaches at Georgia State University; and Kelly Taylor Mitchell, an artist and educator working between Atlanta and San Juan. Photography is part of what this series selects on the museum's own account of the last round — the 2023 jurors “selected a diverse spectrum of artwork including sculpture, painting, photography, textiles and new media”, a show of 46 artists — and the call itself names no medium restriction at all: artists submit three recent works, each produced within the last three years and all of which must stay available for the full run, since a juror may take one piece or several. Images go as jpeg or png under 4 MB and no more than 4800 px on the longest side, new media (video, animation, motion graphics) as mov or mp4 under 25 MB or as a link, with a bio of up to 150 words and a statement of 50–100 words. Work must arrive installation-ready, in what the museum asks be professional-quality frames or mounting. Entry is $35 and up to $5,000 in cash awards is given out. Eligibility is strictly residential: home and studio address both within Georgia, and 18 or over. MOCA GA provides installation staff, pedestals, shelving, projectors and monitors, interpretive materials, press and social marketing, and a public opening reception; artists deliver and collect their own work and sign a museum loan form. Submissions close at midnight on November 1, 2026, selections are notified by December 11, work is dropped off January 7–9 and the exhibition runs January 23 – March 27, 2027, opening with a reception on the 23rd. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Up to $5,000 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: The Aftermath Project 2026 Post-Conflict Grant
item.description: A single $25,000 production grant, free to apply for, from the project Sara Terry founded out of her own five-year body of work on the aftermath of the war in Bosnia: photography that tells “the other half of the story of conflict — the story of what it takes for individuals to learn to live again, to rebuild destroyed lives and homes, to restore civil societies, to address the lingering wounds of war while struggling to create new avenues for peace”. One winner is funded and four finalists are named. The brief is deliberately wide on geography and scale and narrow on subject: the conflict may be an international war, a rebel insurgency, an urban riot or violence between rural ethnic groups, and the Project says it generally looks for stories “no longer being covered by the mainstream media, or which have been ignored”; proposals about the aftermath of domestic violence or environmental disaster are turned away unless clearly framed as the aftermath of conflict. The 2026 letter, signed by interim executive director Andrew Cullen, notes that several recent recipients have worked on conflicts in Ukraine and Gaza that are still running, and that the grant exists so that we “should not look away”. This is a production grant for still photography — explicitly not a distribution grant for exhibitions or books, and grant money may not be spent on video or audio even where a project includes them. An application is a signed form, a two-page proposal opening with a one-sentence summary, a portfolio of up to 30 jpegs (1200 px on the longest side, 72 dpi, under 2 MB each, named LastName_1.jpg), a caption sheet and a two-paragraph bio, sent by WeTransfer, Drive or Dropbox to the Project's email; there is no budget requirement, and it is fine not to have started the project. Open to working photographers worldwide; full-time students are not eligible. Photographers keep all copyright. The winner is paid in three parts — half at onset, 40% at the interim report, the last 10% on delivery of twelve 16x20-inch or larger prints for the Project's archive — with the work due by January 1, 2028 and prints by May 1, 2028; the winner then makes at least 30 images, and finalists 10–15, available for possible exhibition, publication and the Project's lesson plans, with any press-use fee split 50/50 with the photographer. Applications close at midnight PST on December 1, 2026, with the winner and finalists announced by the end of that month. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $25,000.

item.title: Candelar 2027 · Candela Photographic Arts
item.description: A free, deliberately low-ceremony call from Candela, the Richmond photography gallery and independent book publisher that received 501(c)(3) status in May 2026 and reintroduced itself as Candela Photographic Arts “after fifteen years as Candela Books + Gallery”. The Candelar is exactly what the name suggests — a calendar — and 2027 marks its third run: a set of twelve 5×7 inch cards printed in-house on Hahnemühle Museum Etching paper. Candela asks for square photo-based images and frames the brief around the pictures that usually stay in the drawer: “your best and weirdest outtakes, b-sides, one-hit wonders, whatever you wish”. Seasonal themes are welcome but not required, and there is “no theme for the exhibition other than the use of photography”. Up to three square JPEGs at 1500px on the longest side may be entered, each with its title, year, medium and dimensions. Twelve artists are selected, and each receives a copy of the limited-run 2027 Candelar plus an artist’s spotlight on Candela’s website during their Candelar month; accepted artists are notified 23–24 October and the selection is announced Tuesday 27 October 2026. The entry form’s required terms state plainly what the exchange is: a selected image is printed for a calendar set that goes on retail sale, and the copy of that set is the artist’s compensation — no cash, and no transfer of copyright. Submissions are free and run from 29 September to 12 October 2026 at 11:59pm. Candela states no eligibility restriction and names no juror. The call page’s “Submit to the call” button opens a Google Form that requires a Google sign-in; the organiser’s own candelaphotoarts.org/candelar/submit page carries the full terms and a second, un-gated submission form. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print) + contributor copy.

item.title: VCCA Residency at Mt. San Angelo — Fall 2027 Period
item.description: VCCA's Mt. San Angelo campus in Amherst, Virginia takes applications three times a year, and the Fall cycle — for residencies scheduled September to December 2027 — opened on 1 October 2026 and closes 15 January 2027. Photography is one of the disciplines the organisation names outright, alongside poetry, fiction, nonfiction, playwriting and screenwriting, performance, film and video, drawing, painting, sculpture, installation art, music composition and cross-disciplinary art; emerging and established artists may apply, professional training and achievement are not required, and students enrolled in undergraduate, graduate or doctoral programmes are eligible, though projects of pure academic scholarship are not. Mt. San Angelo hosts around 400 artists a year in residencies of no minimum length and up to six weeks, with flexible scheduling. A residency includes a private bedroom with private en-suite bath, a private individual studio, three prepared meals a day and a community of more than 20 other artists in residence; photographers can also request use of VCCA's black-and-white darkroom during the application process. Read the money carefully: one $30 application covers both outcomes. VCCA puts the true cost of a residency at $240 per artist per day, asks accepted artists who do not receive a fully funded fellowship to contribute a minimum of $105 per day, and says it distributes a generous amount of financial aid every year — "if you are accepted and cannot pay at least $105 per day, VCCA will work with you in good faith to be sure you can come" — with reductions granted where true need is demonstrated. The same single application is considered for every fully funded fellowship the applicant is eligible for. Eight are listed for this Fall 2027 period, and the ones open to photographers are the Alonzo Davis Fellowship (American visual artists, two weeks plus a $500 honorarium, preference to those of African or Latin American descent), the Greater Opportunity Fellowships (any discipline, first-time VCCA residents, preference to artists who self-identify as people of color) and the Marian Treger Fellowship for Enduring Creativity (female-identifying visual artists emerging in mid-life and beyond whose paths have been detoured by chronic health conditions or disabilities, two weeks plus a $400 stipend). The application runs on SlideRoom and asks for the form, current work samples and a project description; letters of recommendation are not required. Application fee waivers are granted on request to Artist Services at least five days before the deadline. Artists may be in residence at Mt. San Angelo only once every two years. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: $30. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Life Framer — Solitude
item.description: The December round of Life Framer's twelve-part monthly photography award, judged by Johan Lolos, the Belgian–Greek landscape photographer known for sweeping, emotionally resonant images of the earth's wild places — Alpine peaks, the Gobi desert, the colour-infused Icelandic highlands, the jagged Greek coast. The brief asks for solitude in all its forms: the quiet clarity of a single person, the vastness of an empty landscape, the eloquence of negative space, chosen or imposed, expansive or intimate. Life Framer names a lone person in a crowd, an isolated animal in the wild, empty streets at dawn, minimalist scenes stripped to their essentials and objects set apart from their surroundings, running from contemplative portraits and sparse still life to sweeping vistas and subtle details. All genres and approaches are welcome — documentary, conceptual, candid, staged, studio, environmental — with new work or images from the archive. The award is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers aged 18 and over; the organisers accept all types of photography from analog and digital devices including mobile phones and allow editing, post-processing, mixed media, collage and compositing provided photography is at the heart of the work, but state that they do not accept artificial intelligence or AI-generated imagery. Entry is priced by the number of images: $20 for one, $30 for three, $40 for six, or a $100 membership covering up to ten images in every monthly themed competition for twelve rolling months. The monthly first prize is $2,000, drawn from a $24,000 annual fund shared between the twelve monthly first-prize photographers, and the first- and second-prize images each month are exhibited in galleries around the world. Photographers retain full copyright, and Life Framer states it does not sell usage rights or use entries to train AI algorithms. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: $20–$100. Prize: $2,000.

item.title: Contemporary Horizons · TCG Gallery
item.description: Open-theme international call from TCG Gallery surveying the range of contemporary photography — documentary, portraiture, landscape, still life, abstraction, staged photography and experimental practice all welcome. The gallery frames the horizon as a place, a limit, a possibility or simply a way of thinking about what comes next; a literal horizon is not required, and it says it is equally interested in an intimate observation, a constructed scene, an unexpected formal relationship or a photograph that complicates an ordinary subject. "Contemporary" does not mean an image must have been made this year, follow a trend or depend on a particular camera or technique; suggested approaches run from people, identity and everyday life through places in transition and the built environment to film, alternative processes and experimental photographic methods. Digital, film, alternative-process and mixed-media photographic work is accepted, and previously exhibited work is welcome where the artist retains the necessary rights. Work is reviewed for visual strength, originality, photographic execution and its contribution to a coherent exhibition. Images generated by, or substantially altered with, generative AI are not eligible. Selected photographs appear in a curated online exhibition with artist and artwork information, running 1–31 December 2026, and remain in the TCG Gallery exhibition archive; the show may be promoted through the gallery's website, email and social channels. Submissions take up to three photographs per entry (one is enough, the other two slots optional), JPG at least 1200 pixels on the longest side, unwatermarked; multiple entries are permitted. Sales are optional and the gallery retains a 30% commission on work sold through it. The entry fee is $15 and covers up to three images, with fee waivers available on application — the gallery asks that waivers be requested at least 48 hours before the call closes, i.e. by November 18, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. The prospectus states plainly that it does not promise a printed book, an award or a sale. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $15 (up to 3 images); fee waivers available. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: The Studios at MASS MoCA Residency — July–December 2027 · MASS MoCA
item.description: The Studios at MASS MoCA runs year-round on the museum's North Adams campus, hosting up to ten artists at a time for stays of two or four weeks, and the general open call for residencies between July and December 2027 is live. The programme primarily seeks visual artists — the organisation's own list names painters, sculptors, installation artists, photographers, video and new-media artists, fiber artists and printmakers — alongside writers in all literary disciplines, and artists from around the world are encouraged to apply. There is no application fee, and an artist must be at least 18 to apply; the organisation states that age is otherwise not a consideration in selection. A residency carries a private furnished studio with 24/7 access, a private bedroom in a shared apartment across the street from the museum, one communal meal a day with the other residents, a studio visit with a MASS MoCA or guest curator, optional open studios and presentations, a year of priority access to Assets for Artists career workshops, and three months of museum membership covering free gallery entry and free admission to the nearby Clark Art Institute. Read the money carefully, because one application covers two very different outcomes. The Studios charges rent: the standard rate is $650 per week, already subsidised against a stated operating cost of over $1,000 per week. On the same general application you can ask to be considered for financial aid, where artists "typically pay between $0 – $450/week depending on their needs," and for one or more fully funded fellowships. The General Fellowship is the one with no strings: it "will offer full fellowships that do not have geographic or demographic limitations… regardless of discipline or location," and funds all residency fees for up to four weeks in residence. A Fellowship for Black or Indigenous Artists and Writers funds all residency fees for up to four weeks. A Family Fellowship gives three parent-artists a fully funded August 6–23, 2027 residency with a private three- or four-bedroom apartment, up to two studios with 24/7 access, free reserved places in Camp MASS MoCA for children in grades 2–9, and a $600 stipend. Further partner fellowships are tied to specific communities — the Speranza Foundation (Lincoln City Fellows), YoungArts alumni, Art+Everywhere (MFA graduates of the Art Institute of Boston, Lesley University Art+Design and Clark University), and MFA or BFA fellowships with Brooklyn College, the Corcoran School, Maine College of Art and Design, MassArt, MICA, RISD, SAIC, Tyler at Temple, University of Oregon, UT Austin, Virginia Commonwealth University and Yale. You apply by ticking the relevant box on the general application; there is no separate form, and every applicant must first be accepted through the regular jurying process before a fellowship can be awarded. The organisation asks you to indicate whether you also want to be considered for a regular, partially subsidised residency if no fellowship is awarded — so an unsuccessful fellowship applicant can still be offered a place that costs money. Two routes do NOT lead to a funded place: the Early Application, which gives 9–15 months of lead time but is explicitly for artists planning to fully fund their stay at the $650 weekly rate and is not considered for financial aid or fellowships; and the Alumni application, where returning artists are not eligible for fellowships and pay $400 per week for four weeks or $450 per week for two. Applications close November 1, 2026 at 11:59pm EST. Calls open four times a year, two months before each deadline, with general-application deadlines on May 1 and November 1. The organisation says most residents do not pay the full rate: "The majority of our residents attend with full or partial financial aid." Up to ten images may be uploaded, each under 2MB, or a single PDF of no more than ten pages covering no more than ten pieces; video samples run to ten minutes in total. Notification takes up to three months and comes through Submittable. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Funded residency + $600 stipend (Family Fellowship).

item.title: FORECAST 2026 · SF Camerawork
item.description: SF Camerawork's annual juried exhibition of contemporary photography, presenting work by emerging and under-recognised artists. The jurors for this edition are Janet Delaney, the Berkeley-based photographer of South of Market and a 2020 Guggenheim Fellow; Omar Jason Farah, Curatorial Assistant at BAMPFA, previously at the Leslie-Lohman Museum and the Whitney; and Jonathan Mark Jackson, Assistant Professor of Photography at UC Santa Cruz and a 2026 Hellman Fellow, whose practice joins still photographs and prose around historic Black memory. They will consider all work within the expanded field of photography, from traditional to experimental, with a focus on recently completed, thought-provoking projects. Up to five artists are selected for a group exhibition at SF Camerawork's gallery at Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture in San Francisco, running November 21, 2026 to January 9, 2027. One selected artist receives the $1,500 Juror's Choice Award and up to four more receive a $500 artist fee; selected work is featured across SF Camerawork's media channels, can be sold through the gallery on a 70/30 artist/organisation split, and brings opportunities for artist talks, interviews and audience engagement. Submit up to ten samples of finished, gallery-ready work (images up to 5MB; video up to 5 minutes or 250MB per sample, or a YouTube/Vimeo link), a brief project or artist's statement, and one of a CV, artist résumé or professional biography. Read the access route before you plan: there is NO application fee, but you must be a current SF Camerawork member, with membership valid through the closing date. The Community Membership artist rate is a sliding scale with a suggested contribution of $100 and options starting at $50, open to working artists including students (the full programme value is $250). Join first; the organisation then emails a link to the SlideRoom application, and current members have already been sent theirs. The cutoff is not end of day — applications close Sunday, October 11, 2026 at 5:59 PM PST. Selected artists are notified October 20, 2026 and gallery-ready artwork is due November 14, 2026. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $50+ membership. Prize: $1,500 Juror's Choice + $500 artist fee + Exhibition.

item.title: RC50: A City in Focus · City of Rancho Cucamonga
item.description: Free call from the City of Rancho Cucamonga's RC Public Art Program for a citywide photography exhibition marking the city's 50th anniversary. An Art Selection Panel chosen by the City will pick 50 photographs, each digitally applied to display banners by a third-party vendor and installed in public spaces around Rancho Cucamonga through the anniversary year; selected images may also appear on the project's own website. Every selected photographer is paid a $200 stipend. The City invites photographers of all experience levels and the themes are left to the artist, framed around four prompts: Community (people and everyday moments, neighbourhoods and landmarks, celebrations and traditions), Rancho Cucamonga history, the topography of the land, and nature native to the region. One entry per applicant. Alongside the image, the application asks for a Community Connection Statement of up to 100 words answering "What does Rancho Cucamonga mean to you?" and a three-word completion of the prompt "My Rancho Cucamonga is…"; the statement is scored on how well it communicates the applicant's connection to the city and how closely the work meets the call's goals. Entry is free and the CaFÉ system carries no charge. Read four things before applying. First, the deadline can arrive early: the City states the window closes December 3, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. PDT "or earlier if 200 applications are received (whichever occurs first)." Second, the City's own prospectus states the geographic bar two different ways on the same page — the Artist Eligibility list says "Artist must reside in the Inland Empire region," while the Geographic Eligibility paragraph says "This is an open call, but preference will be given to applicants who work, reside, or attend school in the Inland Empire Region." Third, the rights terms: the artist retains copyright, but the City "owns all installed artwork and reserves the right to copy, reproduce and adjust the artwork as it sees fit, in perpetuity," and reserves the right to remove, replace or adjust the work for the duration of the project. Fourth, the display is not guaranteed in place or duration — banners go onto functioning equipment that may need repair or replacement, and the City issues "no guarantee… for the location or longevity of display." Content limits: no political statements or persons, no religious references or symbols, no copyrighted or trademarked material, no corporate branding, nothing offensive or obscene, and work must be appropriate for public display in civic spaces. Only original photographs are accepted and applicants pledge the image was not digitally altered from someone else's work; artists are responsible for obtaining consent from identifiable people in their photographs. Open to all ages, with parent or guardian permission for minors. Current City employees may not apply. Judging runs January 4–25, 2027 and artists are notified by February 1, 2027. — Deadline: December 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $200 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: PURPLEHAZE PRINT 013 — Unscripted
item.description: Free open call for the Autumn–Winter 2026 printed edition of PURPLEHAZE, an independent Berlin magazine published by HAZE ART & MEDIA GROUP. The theme is UNSCRIPTED, and the editors put it like this: the image does not always begin with intention — sometimes it forms in the space where control loosens, where timing overtakes composition, and where the frame captures more than it can contain. They are looking for work that holds tension, presence and unpredictability, and say they are drawn not only to the captured moment but to work where the process, the material or chance itself leads the artist toward a result that could not have been planned in advance. Staged or not, what matters is whether the work carries the feeling of something uncontrolled. Photographers, painters, performance artists, installation artists and image-makers of all kinds are invited; the call is open to artists worldwide at any stage of their career. Submit up to 12 works or one cohesive series as JPEGs at a minimum of 2000px on the long edge and/or a link to a portfolio or website, with a project statement of up to 150 words and a short artist bio, by email to the magazine. Selected projects appear in the Autumn–Winter 2026 printed edition. On rights: submitting grants PURPLEHAZE non-exclusive rights to reproduce selected work in the issue, and all other rights remain with the artist. Work is reviewed by the PURPLEHAZE editorial team on a separate timeline from the magazine's general submissions, and selected artists are notified by October 15, 2026. Read what does and does not come back before you submit: the magazine's stated policy is that complimentary print copies are not provided for independently selected editorial contributions, and contributors selected through the editorial process receive a 20% discount on one preordered copy of the issue; the magazine also states that publication is never conditional on payment. Previously shared work is welcome for art and photography projects, including work already posted on the artist's own social media — the magazine states that a post on your own account does not count as prior publication. One scope limit to read before applying: the call is for independent editorial and artistic submissions, and projects centred on a single designer, brand, collection, campaign or commercial identity are handled separately through the magazine's partnership formats. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Fotofestiwal Open Program 2027 · Fotofestiwal
item.description: The Open Program is the submissions route into Fotofestiwal, the International Festival of Photography in Łódź, Poland — founded in 2001 as one of the first photography events in Central Europe, visited by more than 20,000 people, and run since 2016 as a collective with no director and no vertical management structure. There is no theme: the organisers say they are looking for artists and collectives with a distinctive personality and for projects that propose a bold and original way of looking at photography and the contemporary world. Work in any technique is accepted, and the call is open with no thematic, age or regional restriction. The jury selects six projects, which are then developed with Fotofestiwal's curatorial team and shown in an exhibition in Łódź in June 2027. Each of the six selected artists receives a €1,000 artistic fee, accommodation for the festival's main opening weekend, travel costs reimbursed up to €300, and a budget of up to €600 for producing the exhibition or transporting the work. At least one of the submitting artists is also nominated to FUTURES, the European platform supporting emerging photographers. The 2027 jury is Jana Johanna Haeckel, curator of the 4th photo+ Photography Biennale in Düsseldorf in 2027 and lecturer in the history of photography and exhibition-making at KASK & Conservatorium in Ghent; Marta Szymańska, a photography curator who has co-created Fotofestiwal for more than twenty years and was deputy director of the Archeology of Photography Foundation from 2014 to 2019; Francesco Rombaldi, curator, editor and book designer, founder of the Yogurt curatorial platform and of Charta; Roï Saade, artist, designer and curator, founder of Huwawa Publishing and director of Bound Narratives, working on visual culture, displacement and cultural production in the Middle East and North Africa; and Krzysztof Candrowicz, co-founder of Fotofestiwal, artistic director of the Hamburg Triennial of Photography from 2013 to 2018 and guest curator of the Ci.CLO Biennial in Porto from 2018 to 2024, who has juried the Rencontres d'Arles Discovery Award, the Deutsche Börse Photography Prize, Prix Pictet and World Press Photo. Submissions are complete photographic projects of 10 to 20 photographs, up to two projects per person, made through Picter. The fee is €15 per project, and the organisers state that a free submission is possible in justified cases — write to opencall@fotofestiwal.com. The call opened on October 1, 2026, closes on November 30, 2026, and results are announced on January 25, 2027. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: €15 per project. Prize: €1,000 artist fee + exhibition + €600 production budget.

item.title: The Room Next Door · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Online juried photography exhibition from Decagon Gallery on the space just beyond what we see — a door left ajar, a window lit across the courtyard, a hallway that turns out of sight, a voice through the wall. The gallery is looking for photographs that bring the viewer to the edge of a space they cannot fully enter: images where something is felt more than shown, where the frame stops just short of an answer, and where what lies beyond is left for the viewer to imagine. The organisers put the distinction plainly — the mystery should come from what the photograph withholds, not from what it hides. Thresholds, doorways, windows and reflections are welcome, as are interiors seen from outside and exteriors seen from within, neighbouring lives glimpsed at a distance, sounds, light and shadows arriving from somewhere else, and constructed or staged work that invents what waits on the other side. Documentary, conceptual and experimental approaches are all accepted; people may appear, but the subject is the space between here and there. Open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over, with all photographic processes and styles welcome. First place receives $500, second $250, third $150 and two honorable mentions $50 each — $1,000 total in cash awards — plus a Human Presence Award granting free entry to a future exhibition of the recipient's choice; cash awards are limited to one per photographer, and a photographer selected for more than one receives only the award of greatest value. Selected artists get an online exhibition by Decagon Gallery, publication in a professionally designed exhibition catalog, and digital badges and certificates. Entry is $25 for up to 4 photographs and $5 each additional, with 10 image slots on the entry form. The juror has not been named: the organiser prints "Juror: TBD". Notification is January 1, 2027 and the exhibition runs January 10 to March 10, 2027. Photographers experiencing financial hardship, living in a war-torn area or residing in a sanctioned country can ask the gallery to waive the entry fee. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $25 (4 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $1,000 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Black and White · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Themed group exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe for monochromatic photography. The gallery's brief is short and direct: before color, there was light and shadow, and black and white photography strips a scene down to its essence, telling stories through contrast, texture and form. They are seeking powerful monochromatic work and ask for your strongest black and white pictures. Juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart, a fine art photographer whose work has been exhibited and published internationally; 26 images are selected for the gallery walls. The gallery covers the whole cost of presentation — one exhibition-quality print on Luster paper, custom framing in the gallery's signature 24×24 inch black museum-quality frames, and matting from its collection of precut white mats, sized by the gallery's team without cropping the original composition. Artists supply only a high-resolution JPEG between 500KB and 5MB with the longest side at 4,500 pixels. The exhibition runs February 5 to 26 with an opening reception on February 5; the year is not printed on the page, but the December 31, 2026 deadline and the two-week notification window place it in 2027. After the show the physical print is archived in the gallery's flat files for six months, photographers retain all rights to their images, and any sale splits 50/50 between gallery and photographer. Acceptance is emailed within two weeks of the deadline and high-resolution files are due within two days of that email. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Entry is $40 for 5 images or $45 for up to 10, non-refundable and stated by the gallery to go towards operational costs. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images, $45/10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Carolyn Harder Scholarship 2027 · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: Annual $1,000 scholarship from the Griffin Museum of Photography, created in memory of Carolyn G. (Grande) Harder (1943-2024) - an art historian, teacher and long-serving docent at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. The award supports emerging photo-based artists and comes with a solo exhibition at the museum in the Fall and a place in Photography Atelier, the museum's year-long project and portfolio development programme. Open worldwide to new photographic artists - students, recent graduates and early-career photographers - with no age limit and no residency requirement. Currently enrolled photography students may apply. Not for well-established photographers: holding a Fulbright or having a photo book published by a publisher disqualifies a candidate, though self-publishing does not. Museum employees, board members and jurors' immediate families are ineligible. Entry is free. The application period for the 2027 cycle opens Monday October 5, 2026 and closes Friday November 6, 2026 at 23:59 Mountain Time; the CaFE entry form takes 5 to 10 images plus a single PDF containing a bio and artistic CV, a statement of artistic purpose and a statement on the work submitted. The museum will announce the awardee by January 1, 2027. The inaugural scholarship went to Cassidy Thurber. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 + solo exhibition + Photography Atelier place.

item.title: Richards Family Prize 2027 · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: A $4,000 scholarship from the Griffin Museum of Photography for mid-career and professional photographers worldwide producing creative, original work. Alongside the cash - intended to assist in the production of the work - the winner receives a catalogue published by Griffin Museum Press and an exhibition at the museum. The museum defines professional as a photographer who earns the majority of their income from photography, and mid-career as one with some visibility in exhibitions, gallery representation, and scholarship or residency success. Its support is stated broadly: fine art to documentary and photojournalism, digital to film-based work and cameraless images, and the call also names installation, moving image and sculpture works. There is no age limit and no residency requirement. Alison Nordström - independent scholar and curator, founding director and senior curator of the Southeast Museum of Photography and former senior curator of photographs at George Eastman House - is the juror for the 2026/2027 cycle. Entry is free. The application period for the 2027 cycle opens Monday October 5, 2026 and closes Friday November 6, 2026 at 23:59 Mountain Time, with 5 to 10 images accepted through the CaFE form; the museum publishes no notification date. Past winners are Izabella Demavlys (2024, Without a Face) and Lee-Ann Olwage (2025, The Right to Play). — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $4,000 + Griffin Museum Press catalogue + exhibition.

item.title: Cartographies of Western and Northwestern Greece · Photopolis Festival
item.description: A free open call from House of Lucie Agrinio, in collaboration with Photopolis Festival and the platform The Provinces, for a photography exhibition at the House of Lucie gallery in Agrinio, Greece, subtitled Human Geography, Land and Landscape. The organisers are looking for images that capture aspects of the landscape of Western and Northwestern Greece, the transformations and changes it is undergoing, and the relationship between people and their environment or aspects of their everyday life — an invitation, as they put it, to give your own visual mapping of these regions. READ THE GEOGRAPHIC GATE BEFORE YOU APPLY: the call is not open-subject, and photographs must come from the specific regional units of Aetolia-Acarnania, Achaea, Elis, Preveza, Thesprotia, Arta and Ioannina. Both amateur and professional photographers may take part, and no age or residency condition is stated — the restriction is on where the pictures were made, not on who made them. Submit 5 to 15 photographs; entry is free. The jury is Eleni Mouzakiti, a photographer, educator and curator with a PhD in Photography from the University of Derby whose work is held in the Portland Art Museum and the Thessaloniki Museum of Photography and who is a founding member of The Provinces; Lila Zotou, a photographer and photography teacher with an MFA from the Utrecht Academy of Arts, based in Oslo and working in new documentary photography and visual narrative; and Panos Kaltsas, founding member and Director of Photopolis Festival, Director of the Streetphotofestival in Athens, and the person in charge of House of Lucie in Agrinio. Selected photographers are notified by email. Files should be 1500 px on the long side and named with the photographer's name in Latin characters followed by 1, 2, 3, and must be sent through a transfer service such as WeTransfer or SwissTransfer — the organisers ask explicitly that you do NOT attach files directly to the email — to photopolisfestival@gmail.com, together with a Word document giving your full name, city, telephone, email, Instagram if you have one, a short text about the photographs you are sending and the location of each one; a short biography is also accepted. You should receive an acknowledgement within 48 hours, and if it does not arrive the organisers ask you to contact them at info@photopolis.gr. On rights: copyright in the photographs remains with their creators, and entrants grant the organisers the right to publish and exhibit the work and post it on social media to promote the event, with the creators named, and with no fee payable for that use. One practical point for anyone outside the area: prints are held at the exhibition space for 30 days for collection in person and are not posted back. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: InFocus Photo Exhibit & Awards 2027: Anything Goes
item.description: The 13th annual InFocus Photo Exhibit & Awards, an Edmonton-based showcase of contemporary photography curated with the stated intention of highlighting voices and perspectives that might otherwise go unseen, and treating photography as both an artistic pursuit and a tool for societal commentary. The 2027 edition is deliberately open-theme — "Anything Goes" — so any subject matter, any style and any genre of photography is eligible, and the call is open to photographers of all skill levels anywhere in the world. Submissions are reviewed by curator and co-founder Alexis Marie Chute, who runs the exhibit under Alexis Marie Productions Inc. Selected work is shown across three Alberta venues — Wild Skies Art Gallery, Red Brick Common Public Art Gallery and Stony Plain Town Hall — through February, March and April 2027, with an opening party in February. Four awards run alongside the exhibition: the organiser says selected photographers are “in the running for the People’s Choice Award and considered for the Emerging Photographer, Landscape, and Portrait Awards”, but what each of those carries in 2027 is not published — the amounts below are the 2026 edition’s, listed on the org’s own homepage under the heading “InFocus Photo Exhibit 2026 AWARDS” beside that year’s named winners. In 2026 the Emerging Photographer Award was a $200 McBain Camera gift card with a plaque and swag; Landscape was a metal print up to 20″×30″ with a plaque; Portrait was a fine art premium canvas up to 24″×36″, a plaque and the winning photo printed in Preview Art Magazine; People’s Choice was a $200 VISTEK gift card with a plaque and swag. None of the four is a cash payment — the two $200 figures are retailer gift cards. Photographers accepted into the exhibition book are paid an honorarium. Accepted photographers are notified within two weeks of the deadline. Fees are in Canadian dollars plus GST and run as a ladder: $25 for the first image, $10 for the second and $5 for each image after that, up to ten images per submission, with unlimited separate submissions allowed. Files are JPG only, maximum 3 MB, named lastname_imagetitle. Two costs to plan for beyond the entry fee: accepted photographers must have their work professionally framed, either themselves or through the exhibit's Pixportal partner, and sales are split 60% to the photographer, 40% to InFocus. — Deadline: October 28, 2026. Fee: CAD $25 first image, $10 second, $5 each additional. Prize: $200 gift cards + Exhibition.

item.title: Innovate Grants - Fall $1,800 Grants
item.description: Two $1,800 quarterly grants for visual artists and photographers — one grant to a photographer and one to a visual artist. Eighteen honorable mentions are also featured and promoted on the Innovate website (nine in art, nine in photo). The application is deliberately minimal: no artist statement, project proposal, or letters of recommendation required — just name, email, grant category, an optional Instagram handle and optional captions, and 3–10 images of recent work. Open globally to visual artists and photographers 18 or over, US and international, in all media and genres; duos, collaborations and collectives may apply. Previous applicants and past honorable mentions may apply again to any new cycle; past grant winners become eligible again five years after receiving their award. Winners and honorable mentions receive feature profiles, interview pages, and promotion to the Innovate Instagram audience of over 73,000 followers. This is the Fall cycle, the fourth of the four Innovate runs each year (Q1 Winter, Q2 Spring, Q3 Summer, Q4 Fall), and it closes at 11:59 PM Pacific on Tuesday 15 December 2026. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $1,800.

item.title: Place and Memory · St. Louis Artists' Guild
item.description: Juried exhibition at the St. Louis Artists' Guild — running since 1886, now in a contemporary gallery and education space at Jackson and Forsyth in Clayton, Missouri — on the spaces that shaped us: the homes left behind, the streets renamed, the landscapes altered, and how memory works as both preservation and transformation. The Guild's framing is that in the tension between fragility and endurance, place lives not only in geography but in the shifting architecture of remembrance. Juror Chris Wubbena is a tenured Full Professor of Sculpture at Southeast Missouri State University with an MFA from San Francisco State, widely exhibited and with public commissions including Spirit of Now in Oak Park, Illinois and Forward in Gulfport, Mississippi. This call's own text names no medium, but the Guild's programme is all-media and demonstrably hangs photographs: the artwork catalogues for its 2026 Members Exhibition and its Ann Metzger National Biennial label pieces “photography”, “black and white archival pigment photograph”, “digital photograph” and “cyanotype”; its sibling call states open to all media and all subject matter; its Executive & Artistic Director Zackary Petot works in printmaking, photography and mixed media; and this call's own upload form accepts GIF, JPG, PNG, MOV and MP4, with the prospectus asking artists to supply their own computer, cords and projectors for work with an electrical component — so photographic, alternative-process and lens-based work is on equal footing. Cash prizes totalling $1,000 are awarded by the juror. Entrants must be 18 or over and resident in the United States; work must be original, completed within the last three years and not previously shown in the Guild's galleries, and priced for sale or marked NFS with an insurance value (the Guild insures 65% of the stated value and takes 35% commission on sales). One application per artist carrying up to three works, submitted as JPEGs a maximum of 1920 pixels on the longest side at 300 resolution, up to 50MB each. Wall-mounted work must not exceed 98 by 84 inches and 40lbs and needs wire and screw eyes, French cleats or another professional hanging device — no saw-tooth hangers, no clip frames — with canvases framed or gallery-wrapped; diptychs and triptychs over the single-entry size count as two or three entries. Accepted work is hand-delivered or shipped at the artist's cost. Entry is $24 for Guild members and $35 for non-members, in both cases for up to three pieces. The exhibition runs 20 November 2026 to 2 January 2027. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $35 ($24 members) for up to 3 works. Prize: $1,000 in cash prizes.

item.title: CON/STRUCT: Images and Identity · York College Galleries
item.description: Free, photography-only juried exhibition at Gallery Hall, Marketview Arts — York College of Pennsylvania's venue in the Downtown York arts district — running 13 November 2026 to 30 January 2027, with an opening reception on 13 November at 5pm. CON/STRUCT examines photography's dual power to actively build identity and enforce social expectations, and the curators read the word for its own tension: the "con" of image fabrication against the rigid "structures" of gender, status and belonging. The show pairs photographs from Ryan Scott Oliver's musical 35mm with a juried selection in the main gallery and an uncurated community wall alongside it, so featured artists and public participants appear together. There are two levels of participation and applicants say which they are applying for: framed, install-ready physical artwork in the main gallery space, or digital images for a repeating slideshow projection in the space adjacent to it — the digital route means no shipping. Curated by Ashley Moog Bowlsbey and Matthew Clay-Robison, director of the York College Galleries. Open to all artists over 18 residing within the United States who work with the photography medium in any form; up to three artworks each, submitted as JPG or JPEG files up to 10MB, sRGB recommended for both black-and-white and colour, named LastName_FirstName_ArtworkTitle_Submission#.jpeg. Submission is free and artists pay only to ship accepted work, which is accepted 6–9 November and must arrive by 9 November; drop-off times and the shipping address are sent on acceptance. Artists are notified by 30 October 2026. The venue is 37 W Philadelphia St, York, PA 17401. One practical warning: the organiser's Google Form is sign-in-gated, so you will need to be logged into a Google account to open it at all — the full terms above are on the call listing, which is readable without one. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Workshop Tunis Edition: Remixing Minor Narratives · Der Greif
item.description: Der Greif, the Munich non-profit for contemporary photography, is running a collective workshop with Jaou Tunis 2026 and selecting its participants by open call. The brief welcomes all photographic genres and themes as long as the submission is a cohesive work-in-progress or completed project that challenges mainstream aesthetics; the open call itself is untethered from any theme. THE GEOGRAPHIC BAR: this call is open only to photographers and lens-based artists based in Tunis and the surrounding areas, and applicants must be available to attend the in-person workshop in Tunis on 26 October 2026, 2pm to 4.30pm, at the B7L9 Art Centre. Selection is by Ilaria Sponda, Der Greif's managing editor and project manager, an independent curator, editor and writer who co-curates Fotodoks and has been a portfolio reviewer for Hamburg Portfolio Review, Sarajevo Photography Festival and Leipzig Photobook Festival. What selected artists get is a place in the free collective workshop inside the Jaou Biennale's official programme, and their work seen by Der Greif's team of experts. Submission is free and is one project of up to 20 images, with the entry form setting a floor of 10; the workshop takes a maximum of 12 participants, all chosen through this open call. Der Greif's conditions of participation are the same non-exclusive terms it uses across its calls: selected artists grant a limited, non-revocable, non-exclusive licence covering inclusion in a Der Greif print publication and display in Der Greif contexts, with credit by name or pseudonym; publication is not guaranteed and no remuneration is paid, but anyone whose work is published in print receives a free copy and every submitter is offered a discount on further copies. Unselected work is archived unless the artist emails to revoke, and remains otherwise unused. Submissions opened 29 September and close 12 October 2026 at 11.59pm CET; results are announced 16 October. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Workshop fellowship.

item.title: International Artist Residency — Autumn 2027 · bEam arts
item.description: One- or two-month studio residency in Thessaloniki, Greece, taking up to five artists from different disciplines per period. Applications for the autumn 2027 cycle close 30 October 2026, with some availability still open for the winter/spring 2027 periods, and decisions are confirmed by 9 November 2026. The 2027 periods run monthly from January to July and again from September to November, and artists staying longer than a month can remain in the studios between periods; the application form also still lists a November 2026 period (4–30 November). Each resident gets an individual studio in a shared space with their own key, continuous one-to-one mentorship and assistance, a well-equipped communal workshop, critiques, visits to museums, galleries and artist studios in Thessaloniki, the chance to propose site-specific projects, presentations or workshops, the chance to exhibit with local venues, promotion through the organisation's social media, and a group exhibition at the end of each residency where work may be sold. Accommodation is optional. bEam arts is an independent, self-funded organisation that receives no external financial support, so the cost sits with the artist: €1,850 for one month with accommodation or €3,300 for two, €1,000 for one month without accommodation or €1,800 for two, with duo artists paying €250 or €150 extra per residency month. There is no application fee; selected artists pay a deposit of 50% of the residence fee, refundable if cancelled 30 or more days before the start date. The organisers encourage applicants to seek funding from national arts councils, foundations or universities, maintain an artist funding directory, and will supply letters of invitation and acceptance and tailored wording for funding applications. Open to artists working in any medium; the application asks for an artist statement and a project proposal of up to 250 words each, plus a CV and 5 to 10 portfolio images with dimensions, technique, title and date. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free (€1,000–€1,850/month if selected). Prize: Residency.

item.title: UNDESCRIBED #12 · DECK Photography Art Centre
item.description: DECK Photography Art Centre describes itself as a non-profit organisation promoting contemporary photography arts and is the organiser of the Singapore International Photography Festival; UNDESCRIBED is its emerging-artist programme, now in its 12th edition. DECK is explicit that this is not simply an exhibition opportunity: the emphasis is on the process of developing a body of work over several months of consultations, critiques, studio visits and conversations with practising artists and arts professionals, with guest artists, curators and gallerists brought in for closed-door feedback sessions. Two mentors accompany the cohort — Robert Zhao Renhui, who has been part of the programme since 2016 and represented Singapore at the 60th Venice Biennale in 2024, and Alecia Neo, whose socially engaged practice foregrounds collaboration, care and radical hospitality rather than the production of objects. The programme culminates in a three-month group exhibition at the Guoco Midtown Public Art Wall in Singapore, opening 25 March 2027. Each selected participant gets S$800 in production support towards developing and presenting the work, a S$300 artist allowance, dedicated consultation time with the mentors, access to DECK's public resources, and curatorial, production, communications and programming support from the DECK team, plus entry to ASG, DECK's network of past and future UNDESCRIBED alumni. The gate is narrow and specific: Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents only, graduates of the 2026 cohort from an art school or arts programme, working with photography, moving image or expanded photographic practices — so this is a call for one year's graduating class, not for emerging photographers generally. DECK also asks that applicants be able to commit to the full schedule, which it publishes up front: onboarding 27 October 2026, project development 20 November, studio visit and feedback 12 December, an industry conversation 20 January 2027, critique and production 18 February, exhibition opening 25 March. Two things to note. DECK's page dates the deadline 20 October 2026, 11:59pm SGT, and repeats it in its Key Dates block, but labels that date a Friday — 20 October 2026 is a Tuesday, and every other weekday label in the block is correct, so treat the weekday as the organiser's slip and the date as the deadline, or apply earlier if you want margin. And DECK's page states no application fee anywhere, but the application form is a sign-in-gated Google Form that cannot be read without a Google account, so the fee could not be confirmed at source — assume nothing and check the form when you open it. — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: S$1,100 support + mentorship + group exhibition.

item.title: Absalon x CPF Photo Print Market · Copenhagen Photo Festival
item.description: Copenhagen Photo Festival and Absalon, the Folkehus — community house — at Sønder Boulevard 73 in Vesterbro, are running their photo print and photobook market again on Sunday 22 November 2026, 10am to 3pm. The festival selects 22 to 24 participants from all submitted proposals, and the market is open to two kinds of applicant: photographers and artists exhibiting prints, and photobook sellers — publishers, vintage book dealers and others. Festival director Maja Dyrehauge Gregersen frames it as wanting to "celebrate what already exists" and, in the name of sustainability, to breathe life into the photo prints sitting in drawers, adding that the market now also opens its doors to photobook publishers showing work in book form. What you get is a table measuring 220 × 85 cm in the hall at Absalon, alongside other photographers, publishers and photo artists, and an audience that comes specifically to buy contemporary photography and photobooks. The festival encourages you to bring a tablecloth and stands to display work on and in front of the table, and to bring work in a range of price ranges. Setup runs from 8am with latest arrival at 9am, and you must deinstall before 4pm. Applying is free, via a form on the festival's own site, but it is a real application rather than a sign-up sheet: the required fields include a PDF with a selection of your prints, the number of prints or books you will bring, your price level, the sizes of your prints, your education and background, your reason for applying, your Instagram tag, and images and a logo the festival can use to promote the market; if you are selected the stall costs DKK 400, payable immediately on receiving the acceptance email, and that amount is non-refundable. One caution on the date. The festival's listing page says both "we are open for applications until 19 October 2026" and, lower down, "Deadline for applications: 20 October 2026" (its Danish line misspells the month). The application page itself states 19 October 2026 twice, in Danish and English. A third block, the form's own intro, still carries 20 February 2026 from the previous edition. Treat 19 October as the deadline. Note also that this is a market, not an exhibition or a juried prize: there is no fee paid to you, no award and no catalogue — you sell your own prints and books and keep what you sell, and you need to be able to get yourself and your work to Copenhagen for the day. — Deadline: October 19, 2026. Fee: Free to apply; DKK 400 stall fee if selected. Prize: Exhibition stall.

item.title: Salong CFF 2026 · Centrum för fotografi
item.description: Centrum för fotografi is Sweden's member organisation for photographers — state-supported, with galleries in Stockholm and Gothenburg — and Salong CFF is its annual open salon, running for the 25th time. It is not a juried competition: every member who registers is hung, simultaneously at three venues, Galleri CFF in Stockholm, CFF in Gothenburg and Galleri kran in Malmö, 20 November to 12 December 2026, with a vernissage at all three on 20 November. The organisation calls it one of the year's most visited exhibitions. Registration is free of charge this year and the only condition is CFF membership. One work per member, a maximum of 50 × 70 cm, registered through a Google Form with a high-resolution JPEG of up to 5 MB that is printed in the salon catalogue — so the image you attach is the image that gets published. CFF also selects one or more of the photographs to promote the salon, asking the artists concerned for approval first. Every work must carry a price and be for sale, with prices including 25% Swedish VAT; CFF takes no commission on sales to private individuals and leaves those sales to the artist, and charges 25% on sales to companies and public institutions. Two things to weigh. You must be able to deliver and collect the work yourself at your chosen venue on the set days — there is no shipping route — so in practice this is for photographers who can get to Stockholm, Gothenburg or Malmö twice. And the membership gate takes time: CFF membership is aimed at professionals working with photographic images, which it defines broadly enough to include photo editors, photo historians and curators, but an application is reviewed before it is approved, and if you have no CV or work online CFF will ask for them separately "in order to make an assessment of your professional experience". Dues are SEK 500 a year, SEK 250 for students, payable after approval, and you can join at any point in the year. No turnaround time for that review is published, and registration closes 18 October — so if you are not already a member, apply well before then. Membership itself carries the usual benefits: open calls, member exhibitions, courses at member rates, a portfolio page and the industry guide. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: Free if you are a CFF member (membership SEK 500/year; SEK 250 student). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Your Best Piece — Open Call · Cut+Paste Magazine
item.description: Cut+Paste is an indie print magazine that pays its contributors, and between its themed quarterly calls it keeps one route permanently open. "Your Best Piece" is exactly what the name says: send a favourite work with no need to align it to a theme. The editors describe it as a way "to give artists flexibility and a chance to submit standout work outside of our regular submission periods", and they accept a wide range of visual art — illustration, painting, photography, graphic design, lettering, digital and traditional media. For photographers the accepted categories are named individually: portraits (faceless preferred), nature and landscapes, abstract and experimental, still life and conceptual, urban and cityscapes, and macro close-up detail. Submitting is free. If work is selected it is paid at the magazine's standard rates — $15 base for photography and graphic design plus, per additional image, $10 full page, $7 for one of two on a page, $6 for one of three and $5 for one of four; art and lettering start at $25. A contributor can opt to have $9 taken out of their payment, plus international shipping, in exchange for a copy of the issue at the magazine's cost. Two things about how this route actually works. It is a slow queue rather than a decision: selected contributors are contacted by email, and a piece that is not chosen immediately "may be kept on file for consideration in upcoming themes", so submitting here puts work in front of the editors for future issues rather than a named one. And there is a rate limit — the magazine asks that artists submit only once every ten days. Files must be high-quality PNG or JPEG. Previously published work is welcome; the editors state that submissions "that have been posted online or elsewhere are still accepted" and that accepted work "can still be posted and sold by the original creator", so no rights are signed away. Not accepted: nudity, foul language, AI art, or work that closely copies someone else's. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + payment.

item.title: 2027 Juried Photography Exhibition · Gallery 14
item.description: Gallery 14, in Hopewell, New Jersey, describes itself as "a co-op gallery of fine art photographers" that shows its members' own work and sponsors shows of other artists and upcoming photographers, and this is the open, all-comers round of its calendar — the annual juried show that fills the gallery for the whole of January. It is photography only: the prospectus states that images "must be originated as a photograph and can't be A.I. generated", which is about as clear a medium gate as a photographer could ask for, and it is the gallery's own sentence rather than a platform's boilerplate. No theme is set, so it is a straight read on the work. Entrants may submit up to eight photographs at $12 for each image submitted, in JPG, with no signatures or other identifying marks on the files. The jury is three people and is worth reading before you decide: Molly Roberts, a documentary photographer and visuals editor whose 35-plus-year career includes The Washington Post Magazine, USA Weekend, Smithsonian Magazine and National Geographic Magazine, and who has taken the NPPA award for Best Use of Photography in a Magazine and been a National Magazine Award finalist; Parvathi Kumar, a fine art and street photographer with recognition from Lens Culture, Life Framer, Exibart and Pure Street Photography, a finalist for the Lucie Foundation, Women Street Photographers and the Istanbul and Brussels street photo festivals, published in the British Journal of Photography, and author of the 2021 photo book Everyday Blackness: Celebrating Exceptional Women; and Nils Huehnergarth, a fine art photographer of candid, street-inspired documentary work whose pictures are in the permanent collection of the New Jersey state capitol in Trenton and who joined the gallery as a member in 2026. Cash awards go to Best in Show, Award of Excellence and Award of Merit, with three further photographs given Honorable Mention; the gallery does not publish the amounts. The exhibition is open to the public Sunday, January 10 to Sunday, January 31, 2027, weekends only, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., with a private awards reception for participating artists and one guest on Saturday, January 9. Two practical things to weigh before entering. First, the prospectus is emphatic that "accepted artists must deliver their ready-to-hang prints to Gallery 14 in person" — drop-off is Friday, January 1, 4-6 p.m. or Saturday, January 2, 10 a.m. to noon, pick-up January 31 or February 1, and while accepted entrants are told they will be sent information about framing requirements and alternative drop-off arrangements, the default assumption is that you can get to Hopewell twice. Second, the gallery takes a 35% commission on sales and all work must be self-insured and stay up for the full run. Selections are notified by November 30, 2026. Submitting also grants the gallery permission to use accepted images, with an artist credit line, on its website and in printed material promoting the show. The curator is Rebecca DePorte. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $12 per image. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Center Fellowship 2027 · Center for Art & Advocacy
item.description: The Center for Art & Advocacy's flagship fellowship — founded in 2017 by the artists Jesse Krimes and Russell Craig, and known until recently as Right of Return — gives $20,000 to each of six formerly incarcerated artists: $10,000 in unrestricted funds and $10,000 in project development funds. It is the first fellowship of its kind in the United States. Fellows join an annual retreat where they present their project proposals to the cohort, take feedback from their peers and meet previous fellows, advocates, industry leaders and funders, with time built in for New York City's cultural calendar. For the first time, one of the six places is reserved for an artist aged 18 to 24. Photographers are in scope on the Center's own evidence: it describes its 2023 Fellow Beverly Price as a "fine art photographer whose work focuses on the intersection of preventative justice and critical compassion" and its 2024 Fellow Antwan "Banks" Williams as "a published photographer", and the call itself invites creatives working in visual art, film, music, creative writing, performance, design and multidisciplinary practices — every discipline, in the organiser's words. Who can apply: artists directly impacted by incarceration, meaning those who have themselves been held in US prisons, jails or detention centers (applicants detained in migrant detention centers must have attained US citizenship by the time applications opened), aged 18 or over, at any career stage, with or without formal training. Individual artists only, no organisations or non-profits. Projects and applicants must be US-based, including all fifty states, Washington DC and Puerto Rico. Fellows must collaborate with an advocacy organisation while developing or executing the proposed project, though that partner does not need to be secured at the time of application — the Center will help connect fellows to advocates. A panel of external reviewers selects the cohort. Applications opened September 18, 2026 and close Sunday, October 25 at 11:59 PM; the cohort is announced publicly on January 12, 2027. There is no application fee. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $20,000 × 6 fellows.

item.title: Light of a Clear Blue Morning · Kinhouse Gallery
item.description: A winter solstice group show at Kinhouse Gallery in Fort Wayne, Indiana, taking its title in spirit from Dolly Parton's song about weathering hard seasons and trusting that brightness returns. The gallery is not asking for cheer: the call is an invitation to sit with the dark honestly, without rushing past it, and to find or make the soft, luminous things that help us through it. Work is wanted on the solstice as a threshold between darkness and returning light; on hope that is hard-won rather than naive; on softness as a form of resilience — comfort, warmth, tenderness, rest; on literal or symbolic light, from candles and lanterns to dawn, fire and the glow that persists in low light; on ritual and gathering, and how communities get through winter together; and on quiet interior or domestic scenes that hold beauty in small, unremarkable moments. Photography is named in the gallery's own list of welcome media alongside painting, drawing, textile, ceramics, printmaking, sculpture, fiber art and mixed media, and the page adds that all art mediums are accepted for consideration; Kinhouse says it is especially drawn to work that embraces softness in both subject and material. Fifteen dollars covers up to three entries, an entry being one work however many images represent it, and fees are non-refundable. Every selected artist receives a $20 shipping stipend — more than the entry fee — plus a place in the brick-and-mortar gallery and on the Kinhouse Instagram. Work does not have to be for sale, though the gallery prefers it; if it sells, the commission is 20% and the artist keeps 80%, paid within two weeks of the show closing. Artists ship the work both ways at their own cost unless it sells. Open to people of any gender identity and any ability, but because of recent global shipping problems this edition is restricted to artists shipping to and from the United States and Canada. Work must be finished, not in progress, and must arrive at the gallery by November 30. Notifications go out by November 3, and the show runs from early December to January 22, 2027 — the gallery's own page dates the opening reception Friday, December 2, while its CaFE listing says Friday, December 4, which is the date that is actually a Friday. — Deadline: October 26, 2026. Fee: $15 for up to 3 entries. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Contemporary Indigeneity 2027 · Great Plains Art Museum
item.description: The sixth iteration of the Great Plains Art Museum's juried exhibition for Native American artists, at the Center for Great Plains Studies on the University of Nebraska–Lincoln campus. The museum is looking for work addressing any theme relevant to the contemporary Indigenous experience on the Great Plains — a region the Center defines loosely as stretching westward from the Missouri River at Omaha and Kansas City to the Rocky Mountains, and northward from the Texas Panhandle into the Canadian Prairie Provinces. There are no limitations on artwork media, so photographic work is eligible on the museum's own terms; the practical constraints are physical, with two-dimensional work capped at 70 inches on its longest side including the frame and three-dimensional work at 135 inches of length and girth combined and 100 pounds. A panel of Native American art professionals reviews the submissions and selects on aesthetic merit and contribution to the field of contemporary art; the 2024 edition's panel was Mary V. Bordeaux (Sicangu Oglala Lakota) of Racing Magpie, Dr Chelsea M. Herr (Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma) of the Gilcrease Museum, and Tarah Hogue (Métis) of Remai Modern, which gives a sense of the level. It is free to apply. Each artist may submit up to three works, though not all submitted works will necessarily be shown. Work must be original, created during or after 2025, never previously exhibited at the museum, and available for the whole run. Applicants must be Native American artists and will be asked in the application for proof of tribal enrollment or descendancy documentation, and must be 18 or over at the time of submission. A limited number of works are purchased from the exhibition for the museum's permanent collection, chosen by museum staff on the jurors' recommendations, with purchase-award notifications between September 30 and October 31, 2027; work is not listed for sale while on view, but staff will connect an interested buyer with the artist. The museum pays all incoming and outgoing shipping — the artist pays only for presentation (matting, framing). Acceptances are announced April 1, 2027, work is delivered between July 15 and August 16, and the exhibition runs September 3 to December 18, 2027. The museum and the Center describe the show as central to a standing commitment to increase the representation of Native artists in their collections, exhibitions and educational programs. — Deadline: February 5, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Museum exhibition + Purchase awards (cash).

item.title: 26th Images of the Virgin · Luna Gallery and Eco Art Studio
item.description: Luna Gallery and Eco Art Studio in San Juan Bautista continues an exhibition with a real lineage: the annual Images of the Virgin show that Galeria Tonantzin ran from 1992 to 2012. This is the 26th edition of that exhibition, counting the whole lineage rather than Luna's own run of it. The call asks for work exploring the many manifestations of the virgin, mother and goddess in her visual forms — traditional and provocative, across cultures, including the Virgen de Guadalupe. Photographers are named in the hanging rules alongside painters and printmakers: painting, prints, photos and multimedia must be wired ready to hang with a maximum width of 48 inches, and sculpture must fit a 12 by 12 inch pedestal or stand free. Up to three pieces for a $35 entry fee, or $30 if you are a gallery affiliate member, and one entry per artist. The juror is Maya C. Ramirez, a PhD student in the History of Visual Arts and Cultures at UC Santa Cruz whose research covers religious mythology, gender and mysticism, and queer theological perspectives; her essay on Fabián Cháirez and queer Catholic symbology appeared in Tufts University's journal Ekphrasis. Entry is by email to lunaecoart107@gmail.com with one to three digital images plus title, media, price and contact details — payment instructions come back by reply — or through the gallery's EntryThingy page. Selected work ships to the gallery's PO box by November 20 or is hand delivered on November 21 or 22 between noon and 4pm, in reusable packaging with return postage; shipping and insurance are the artist's cost and the gallery takes 40% on sales. The exhibition runs November 28, 2026 to January 10, 2027, with the reception and conference on December 12 and pick-up on January 10. Luna Gallery is a non-profit running a gallery and an eco-art teaching studio, and no cash award is attached to this show. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: $35 for up to 3 works ($30 gallery affiliate members). Prize: None listed.

item.title: Little Luxuries 2027 · Main Line Art Center
item.description: Now in its third year, Little Luxuries is Main Line Art Center's small-works show — a regional juried exhibition of 100 artists chosen by a guest juror, built deliberately as an accessible entry point for new collectors and a way for them to find artists they don't know yet. Nothing may exceed 10 inches in any direction including the frame (the Center measures work at drop-off and says there will be no exceptions), everything must be for sale and priced under $350, and up to three pieces may be submitted for $15. Work must be original — reproductions and prints of existing work are not accepted, and neither is AI-generated art. Works on paper must be framed, and everything arrives ready to display with hanging hardware. The show runs 16 January to 19 February 2027 in the Center's gallery in Haverford, outside Philadelphia, opening with a ticketed collector preview from 4 to 6pm on 16 January followed by a public reception. Sales are split 60% to the artist, 40% to the Center. There is no prize. On the medium question, read the invitation for what it is: the call says only that "artists working in all mediums are encouraged to apply" and neither the call page, the SlideRoom application, nor the previous edition's exhibition page enumerates media or names photography — so a photographer has an open door rather than a guarantee. What supports taking it seriously is the Center's own practice: photography is one of the media categories in its class catalogue (Digital Arts & Photography), and its Betsy Meyer Memorial Exhibition names photography outright among the accepted categories. Small prints, alternative-process work and anything that reads at 10 inches are the obvious fit. Non-local artists are explicitly accommodated — accepted work can be shipped at the artist's expense to arrive by 7 January, with the artist responsible for insuring it in transit — so "regional" describes the show's centre of gravity rather than a residency bar. Drop-off is 6 or 7 January, pick-up 20 and 22 February. The Center does not publish a notification date. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Exposure One Awards - Nature Photography Contest 2026
item.description: Exposure One's black-and-white nature contest, running for the first time as a separate cycle alongside the platform's Photographer of the Year and One Shot contests. Thirteen categories — Abstract, Aerial, Animals, Earth's Textures, Humans & Nature, Land, Light & Shadow, Minimalism, Ocean, Pattern & Form, Underwater, Wild Portraits and Other — and the organisers encourage an expansive reading of each; one image may be entered in several categories and is judged independently in each. Black and white only, with sepia and other single-tone images accepted. There is no cap on how many images you may submit, and a series is 2–5 images working within one concept. Prior publication, prior awards and work of any age are all fine; the contest does not require exclusivity. Over $4,000 in cash awards, plus an online winners' gallery, a profile in the Exposure One artist directory, a published interview in Exposure One Magazine, a custom press release, badges and certificates, and the option to buy a trophy. Judged by five institutional jurors. AI-generated images are not admissible in any Exposure One contest, and the organisers reserve the right to ask for proof of original files. The entry ladder runs from $15 for a student single image to $50 for a professional series, with 15% off during early bird (to 11 November) and 10% off in the regular round (to 8 December); additional categories are half price, and 5- and 10-credit bundles cut the per-entry cost further. The published schedule runs early bird to 11 November and regular entry to 8 December 2026, with winners announced 20 January 2027 — 8 December is the last date the organiser prints anywhere on the page, and it is the date stored here. The page's underlying schedule data also carries an extended round to 5 January 2027, but the organiser keeps that round hidden on this contest where it publishes it on its sister contests, so treat 8 December as the deadline and do not plan around a later round that has not been announced. — Deadline: December 8, 2026. Fee: $15–$50. Prize: $4,000+.

item.title: CONNECTION · Full Circle
item.description: Free open call for emerging artists for CONNECTION, an exhibition at Full Circle in Ixelles, Brussels, staged as part of the 2026 Ideas Festival, whose theme is the same word. The brief reads connection broadly — intimacy and relationship, community and belonging, technology and its paradox of closeness and distance, ancestry and heritage, the body's connection to environment, and the quiet internal connection between self and identity — and the organisers name Marina Abramović, Félix González-Torres, Judy Chicago, Andy Goldsworthy and Do Ho Suh as points of departure. Literal, abstract, personal and political readings are all welcome.
