The call says it invites "artists working in various media"; it does not enumerate media and photography is not named on either the call page or the seven-page terms document, so a photographer should read the open wording as an invitation rather than a guarantee — though the terms do require a model release for any identifiable person depicted, and a signed parental release for anyone under 18, which is a lens-based requirement. Eligibility is set by the terms: artists must be at least 18 on the date of application, there are no nationality or residency requirements, and the call is aimed at artists who "must not or rarely be presented in other exhibitions", in the spirit of emerging artists who have not yet had much chance to show. More than one entry may be submitted. Everything is judged from digital files — physical works are submitted as digital images — and each work needs a title, a size, a description of its medium and a statement of its relationship to the theme, alongside an artist statement covering the work, the artist and their wider practice. AI work is acceptable but must be identified as such. There is no entry fee. Selected works may be offered for sale at a price the artist sets, with Full Circle taking a 30% commission; the artist carries the risk of damage or loss and is advised to arrange insurance, and work must be transportable by the artist and able to get into the venue. Entrants also grant Full Circle a promotional licence to reproduce exhibited works in connection with the exhibition. Every candidate is told the jury's decision by email on 5 November 2026 — the date the terms give, though they label it a Friday and 5 November 2026 is a Thursday. The show runs 20–30 November 2026, with the call page also describing works staying on view on selected dates until early January. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition at Full Circle, Brussels, with works offered for sale at the artist's price (30% commission).

item.title: ArtDepå 2026 · Konstepidemin
item.description: First edition of ArtDepå, a selling exhibition at Gröna Rummet, Konstepidemin, Gothenburg, running 4–13 December 2026. The organisers describe it as a living, off-line circulation platform for artworks that already exist: almost every artist has an archive of their own work in the studio — sketches, tryouts, works made for public or private contexts, works that were shown once or never found their way into a gallery — and ArtDepå exists to give those works a chance to be seen and sold. The presentation is deliberately dense and maximalist, spread across walls, tables, stands and vitrines to encourage browsing and unexpected discoveries. Photography is explicitly among the welcome media, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture and objects, ceramics, textile, jewellery and other physical work suited to the format. The call is aimed at professional artists; those based in Gothenburg and surrounding municipalities are particularly encouraged, but applications from elsewhere are welcome. 20 artists are chosen through a jury process that weighs artistic quality and a diversity of media and approaches befitting ArtDepå's character; the jury is Mona Wallström and Ami Norda, with Jelizaveta Suska as selection coordinator — the application form names all three, while the call page omits Ami Norda. (The organisers' own blurb says the show will gather works by 30 artists while the Selection section states 20 will be chosen — the page contradicts itself on that number in both its English and Swedish texts.) The application asks for a one-page A4 CV, a biography and an artist statement of up to 500 characters each, five images of representative works with title, year, medium and dimensions, links to website and Instagram, and contact details; the form also asks roughly how many works you expect to bring. Konstepidemin's page lists F-Tax registration — a Swedish business tax registration — among the application items, but the live application form neither lists it nor provides a field for it, so it is not a gate on applying from outside Sweden; where it is likelier to matter is invoicing a sale. There is no application fee and no participation fee; ArtDepå takes a 30% commission on sales, and every included work must be available for sale, labelled with the artist's name, title, contact and price. Selected artists may bring up to 100 artworks each and are responsible for transport, packaging, making work installation-ready, and their own insurance — the organiser does not insure participating works and, under the participation agreement, is not liable for theft, loss or damage except in cases of gross negligence. Selected artists are notified 14 October 2026. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition at Gröna Rummet, Konstepidemin, with works offered for sale (30% commission).

item.title: McClure Gallery 2027–28 Exhibition Programme
item.description: The McClure Gallery, the exhibition arm of the Visual Arts Centre in Westmount (Montreal), is accepting submissions for its 2027–28 exhibition programme. Contemporary artists working in all media, and curators with an exhibition proposal, are invited to apply — photography is covered by that all-media opening, and the gallery's only stated technical caveat is that it has limited A/V equipment and may not be able to support certain new-media works. Proposals are reviewed by a committee of peers that is renewed every year, and selected projects may be shown in one or both of the gallery's two adjoining exhibition spaces. The gallery pays CARFAC-based artist exhibition rights fees (A.1.1 for solo, A.1.3 for group shows), so selected artists are paid rather than charged. Submission is free and has two parts: a completed online submission form, and a dossier sent as a single WeTransfer to the gallery containing 10–20 JPG images (max 1.5 MB each) and/or links to video excerpts of up to eight minutes of recent work, plus three separate PDFs — an image list giving artist name, title, year, medium and dimensions in centimetres; a CV of no more than three pages; and a description of your practice and proposed project of no more than two pages. File naming is prescribed to the letter (01InitialsYearTitle.jpg; lastname_list.pdf, lastname_cv.pdf, lastname_project.pdf), images must not be embedded in a PDF — proposals submitted as a single PDF are not evaluated — and dossiers emailed as attachments rather than sent via WeTransfer are not accepted. The gallery's two surfaces disagree on that last point: the submissions page rules out a single-PDF proposal and email attachments, while the confirmation item on the live entry form asks for the documents "via WeTransfer or as one compiled PDF" sent to the gallery mailbox. One WeTransfer satisfies both readings. Cover letters, press materials and any extra images are not forwarded to the jury. The gallery asks that your proposal say why you want to show at the McClure specifically, in keeping with the Visual Arts Centre's mandate. It prioritises submissions from contemporary artists living in Quebec but explicitly does not exclude artists from other provinces or countries. Artists who have had a solo exhibition there in the past five years are asked to wait before proposing again. Applicants are told by email of the committee's decision in approximately three months. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + CARFAC exhibition fee.

item.title: Walk of Water Photostory Contest: Out of Sight · Onewater
item.description: Sixth edition of the Walk of Water Photostory Contest, run by Onewater with UNESCO's World Water Assessment Programme, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and other partners, with a US$9,000 cash prize pool. The theme, "Out of Sight", covers water and health in the widest sense — how water shapes health, longevity and well-being — and points its brightest light at the part nobody photographs: wastewater. The organisers name dignified toilets, clean rivers and the damage untreated sewage does to people and ecosystems, and they single out wastewater surveillance — sampling at treatment plants, drains, hospitals, airports and transport hubs, laboratory analysis, data interpretation and the public-health response — as "stories that almost never get photographed, because nobody commissions them". But the brief is explicitly wider than the pipe: the river that cools a city, the ritual bath, the swimming lesson, the tap that finally runs safe, the mental-health and spiritual value of blue spaces, sport and active living in pools, lakes and coasts, and safe drinking water, sanitation and hygiene across homes, workplaces, schools and care facilities all belong. A submission is a photo story: 5–10 photographs (JPG, at least 10 megapixels, long side 3,872 px or more, sRGB recommended), a written narrative, numbered captions and a signed photo licence (entrants under 18 need a parent or guardian to co-sign). The organisers state the narrative length twice and differently on the same page: one copy of the How to enter block asks for a narrative of 2,500–8,000 characters and captions of 30–300 characters each, the other for a narrative of 100–400 words with no caption range, so allow for either until they settle it. Up to three photo stories per participant, no more than one prize per participant. The pool splits into two tracks: the Global Wastewater Award (US$6,900 — $3,000, $2,000, $1,000 and three US$300 merit awards, each with a feature on the Onewater website) and the Youth Wastewater Award (US$2,100 as the organisers label it, though the six youth prizes they list — $900, $750, $250 and three of $200 — add up to $2,500) for photographers aged 25 or under on 1 December 2026, judged across the full Out of Sight theme. Beyond the money, the strongest stories of the edition — wastewater or not — are shown in the 2027 Walk of Water exhibitions and published with Onewater's media partners worldwide. Judging weighs visual storytelling, originality, photographic quality, writing, relevance to the theme and the strength of the connection drawn between water, ecosystems and human health; the jury's decision is final and scores are not shared. AI-generated images are not accepted — the rules ask for photographs, and permit only basic adjustments (dust removal and the like), not adding or removing picture content. One term deserves reading before you enter: submitting means licensing the photographs and the story under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 (CC BY-SA 4.0). By submitting your work to the competition and signing the Photo Licence Agreement, you grant Onewater and the contest's convenors, partners and sponsors a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide and permanent licence to use and adapt your photographs and stories. They may use your work, including commercially, to promote the contest, its exhibitions and you as a photographer, to raise funds, and for their water-related, or social and environmental impact work. Press, exhibition venues, cultural institutions and agencies may also use your work, but only in partnership with Onewater or a convenor. Your work may be edited, for example cropped, combined with text or logos, or have its texts shortened or translated, but its original meaning or message will not be changed. You will always be credited, and your work will not be used to train artificial intelligence. You keep your copyright and remain free to sell and license your photographs elsewhere. You confirm that the work is your own and that everyone identifiable in it has agreed to be shown. Entries open 1 October 2026 and close 30 November 2026 at 23:59 CET; winners are announced in January 2027. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: US$9,000 cash total — Global Wastewater Award $6,900 ($3,000 + $2,000 + $1,000 + 3 × $300) and Youth Wastewater Award $2,100.

item.title: Abstract Mind 2027 — 12th International Exhibition on Abstract Art · CICA Museum
item.description: The twelfth edition of CICA Museum's international abstract-art exhibition, at the contemporary art museum in Gimpo, South Korea, open to artists worldwide. The museum is looking for work that explores abstraction, Abstractivism, and the expression of the mind and of abstract concepts — and photography is named first among the welcomed media, with "Photography & 2D Digital Art" one of four submission categories alongside painting/drawing/print, sculpture and installation, and video and interactive art. Submission is free and by email: up to five JPEGs (100–500 KB recommended) and/or up to three direct links to video works, plus a bio, with the subject line "Submission: Abstract Mind 2027 – Category – Artist's Name". Selected photographic and 2D digital work is printed by the museum at 10 × 15 or 10 × 10 inches, framed and installed by its curators and assistants; larger prints can be requested and may carry additional fees. Artists sending physical work ship it both ways at their own cost, with 2D pieces capped at 39 inches (1 m) on the longest side, installation at 39 × 39 × 79 inches and wall-mounted work at 10 kg. Accepted artists contribute $78 USD (110,000 KRW) per work toward exhibition processing and maintenance to confirm participation — the same structure as the museum's other group calls. The show runs May 19 – June 13, 2027, and the museum notes the dates are subject to change. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: Free to submit; $78 per accepted work. Prize: Museum exhibition.

item.title: Working With Paper · Mosaic Art Collective
item.description: Juried group show at Mosaic Art Collective, the nonprofit gallery and community hub at 410 Chestnut Street in Manchester, New Hampshire, built around paper as both material and subject. The collective's framing: paper is a simple material with deceptively vast possibilities, and despite technological advances it remains ubiquitous — lists, notes, letters, everyday information — and that simplicity is what holds the potential. Works may be two or three dimensional, and the collective's own examples are drawings, paintings, origami and papier mache "or any number of combinations of practice"; paper as a material and paper as a subject are both welcome, but every work must incorporate actual paper. Photography is not named in that list, and it is not excluded either — the only stated material rule is the actual-paper requirement, so a photogram, cyanotype, paper negative, chine-collé or folded or collaged print answers the brief on its face, while a digital print pinned behind glass may not; photographers should expect to make the paper itself part of the work. Photography does appear in the gallery's own programme — its current exhibition text describes works on view "spanning photography, painting, sculpture, video, installation, and mixed media." Reproductions and AI-generated content are excluded. Entry is $10 for the first work and $10 for each additional, up to three, so a full submission costs $30, and the call runs through the collective's own Crafted Call platform. Acceptances go out Sunday, November 1, 2026; work is dropped off in person on 4, 5 or 6 November between 4 and 6pm, which in practice makes this a call for artists who can reach Manchester. The exhibition runs 14 November – 23 December 2026, opening with a reception on 14 November, 5–7pm. All work must arrive ready to hang with proper wire; there is a $5 wiring fee at drop-off if yours is not wired, and uncollected work incurs a $10 a day storage charge. Sales carry a 25 per cent gallery commission, so the artist keeps 75 per cent. There is no cash award; the return is the exhibition. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: $10–$30. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Griots: Our Stories, Ourselves · The Art Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at The Art Center at Johns Creek, Georgia, about storytelling and who gets to do it — opening on the African proverb "Until the lion learns to write, every story will glorify the hunter." The brief takes the West African griot — storyteller, historian, musician and keeper of cultural memory — as its starting point and argues that artists are storytellers too, using paint, photography, sculpture, fibre, ceramics, printmaking and mixed media to preserve memory, give voice to experience and offer new ways of seeing. It welcomes work on personal narratives, family histories, cultural traditions, identity, place, migration, heritage, memory, community, social experience or imagined futures, told directly or through symbolism, metaphor, abstraction, materials or visual language; the curators name Mardi Gras Indian traditions, Gullah culture, the African American church, African American folklore and Afrofuturism as examples rather than limits. Photography is explicitly among the eligible media, alongside mixed media, ceramics, drawing, fibre art, printmaking, painting, collage, digital art and sculpture, and the list is "not limited to" those. The entry form's own Accepted Media menu is the one place photography is missing — its options are painting, drawing, printmaking, fibre art, mixed media, ceramics, sculpture, digital art, metalwork, woodworking and Other — so a photographic entry is filed under Other, and the prospectus gives the curator's address for questions about a particular medium. Each submitted work must come with a short paragraph on how it relates to the theme; the statement is weighed in the jurying and used in the gallery. AI-generated work will not be considered. Entry is $30 non-refundable for one application carrying up to five works. First Place is a $500 cash award, with further cash awards and recognitions whose total depends on the number of submissions and sponsorship raised. The Art Center is a nonprofit and says the lion's share of entry fees goes to the exhibition and its participating artists. Notification is January 16, 2027; the show runs February 3 – March 6, 2027. — Deadline: January 9, 2027. Fee: $30. Prize: $500 First Place.

item.title: FLOAT Magazine — Open Submissions
item.description: Year-round, free submissions to FLOAT Photo Magazine, an independent photography publication that runs printed issues alongside online features, online exhibitions, artist portfolios, book reviews and Instagram takeovers. All photographic styles are accepted; the editors are looking for cohesive, thought-through bodies of work, for both the online content and the magazine issues. The online-portfolio route asks for 10–25 images from a single body of work as JPEGs at 1200 pixels on the long side, plus an artist statement or relevant text with a title and description of the work and a link to your website — files must be attached, not sent via WeTransfer, which the team says often expires before they download it. Separate routes exist for an Instagram takeover (send your Instagram link, username and a self-portrait; if selected you supply up to 12 images with captions, though the waiting list is long) and for a book review (send the full book PDF with 1–5 images; if a contributing writer picks it up you mail them a physical copy, which is not returned). Everything goes by email to floatzine@gmail.com. Work not selected can be resubmitted later with a different body of work. FLOAT is volunteer-run and says it cannot always reply to every email, and it publishes no notification window. This is the magazine's standing submissions policy, separate from its occasional themed printed-issue calls, which charge a fee. One caution: the same page still advertises the themed issue call Let's Get the F@!#k Outta Here as upcoming, with a link to submit, but that $9 call closed on its own page in July 2026. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Photo of the Season — Calm Before the Storm · The Image Flow
item.description: The autumn cycle of The Image Flow's quarterly Photo of the Season competition, themed Calm Before the Storm — quiet images full of tension, where what counts as a storm is left to the photographer: extreme weather, a high-stakes performance, a protest, a party, or something unnamed. The Image Flow is a photography gallery, print lab and education space at 328 Sir Francis Drake Boulevard in San Anselmo, California, and judges in house on composition, colour, contrast and overall quality alongside subject interest, point of view and whether the image tells a story. Open to photographers worldwide, amateur and professional. $15 for up to three images. First place $150, second $100, third $50; the call page promises three honorable mentions where the terms page still says two. All winners and honorable mentions are featured in the gallery's newsletter, website and social media, and selected images from all four 2026 seasons are shown together in a group exhibition at The Image Flow in 2027 — if an exhibited print does not sell, the artist collects it or pays return shipping, and unclaimed prints are recycled after 30 days. Eligible media are analogue film, digital, alternative process, printmaking and digital art; movies/video and AI-generated images are excluded, and the two surfaces disagree on mixed media — the call page excludes it outright while the terms page admits photography-based mixed-media. The terms also bar overt sexual content or graphic nudity, political imagery and religious iconography, and violent, sorrowful or disturbing subjects including images of weapons — a restriction worth reading before paying, since the call's own prompt offers a protest as one possible storm. Submissions opened September 22, 2026 and close Monday December 21, 2026 at 11:59 PM; artists are notified by email and no notification date is published. — Deadline: December 21, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: $150 / $100 / $50 + exhibition.

item.title: Silence · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Curated international group photography exhibition on silence — a state the gallery sets against sound, noise and loudness, and reads in two directions at once: loneliness, alienation and a disturbing unknown landscape on one side, known tranquillity and peace on the other. The call points to the photographic contrast between deep darkness and dazzling light, to what falls silent after natural or social catastrophe — empty cities, villages, abandoned public transport, empty workplaces as reminders of the transience and fragility of humankind — and to the quiet activities of contemplation and meditation that negate the nature of action itself. Silence is noted as present in still lifes, cityscapes, portraits and many other photographic genres, and the theme is broadly construed without any photographic genre restrictions. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD in Philosophy, Rutgers; founder, director and curator of PH21 Gallery, a Photolucida Critical Mass juror since 2023 and invited to Photolucida's board in 2026) and Borbála Jász (art historian and philosopher of art, PH21 vice-director, a Critical Mass juror since 2025 and also invited to the board in 2026). One curator's choice and up to three honourable mentions are announced; the curator's choice receives three free entries to any upcoming PH21 themed group call, each covering up to 15 images. Entrants may submit 3, 5, 7, 10 or 15 images, individual works or a series of at most five photographs, by email after paying the fee. A reduced rate of €15 (early bird) or €20 covers up to five images for students, unwaged applicants and those from low-income economies — the gallery asks for no proof of eligibility and says it trusts the applicant's judgement. Early bird deadline November 2, final deadline November 9; all entrants are notified 10–15 days after the final deadline. The exhibition runs January 19 – February 2, 2027 at PH21's venue in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter. Selected photographers pay a print and installation fee, from €45 for prints up to 40cm on the longest side, or may ship their own exhibit-ready prints; work need not be for sale, and the gallery commission on any sale is 25%. — Deadline: November 9, 2026. Fee: €25–€50. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 20th Biennial Joyce Elaine Grant Photography Exhibition · Texas Woman's University
item.description: The twentieth edition of the biennial Joyce Elaine Grant Photography Exhibition, a national juried show at Texas Woman's University's East | West Galleries in Denton, running February 15 – March 12, 2027. Established in 2001 by TWU and the Photographic Artists' Coalition, a student-run photography organisation, JEG was founded by alumna Christine Shank and a small group of graduate students and named in memory of the mother of Professor Susan kae Grant, Cornaro Professor of Visual Art Emerita. Every edition is juried by a distinguished female curator; this one is judged by Maria L. Kelly, Assistant Curator of Photography at the High Museum of Art in Atlanta, who has helped organise nearly thirty photography installations there — among them Photography's New Vision: Experiments in Seeing (2025), Tyler Mitchell: Idyllic Space (2024), Underexposed: Women Photographers from the Collection (2021) and Helen Levitt: In the Street (2015) — and has curated at Friche la Belle de Mai in Marseille, Emory University, Swan Coach House Gallery and Columbus State University. Beyond selecting the group show, the juror awards one artist a solo exhibition in the TWU East | West Galleries, scheduled during the following JEG Exhibition. Open-themed and open to photographers, lens-based or lensless, video and photo-related artists based in the United States; all photographic and related processes are encouraged, including digital, video, non-silver, photo and mixed media, and photographic book arts. Work must not exceed 60 inches in any dimension. Judging is online from JPEGs of at least 1200 pixels on the longest side and no more than 5 MB; one to five images cost $35 (Basic Application) and up to ten cost $60 (Expanded Application), with fees non-refundable and treated as donations to the JEG Endowment, which funds photography scholarships for TWU graduate students. Accepted artists are notified by December 9, 2026, pay their own shipping both ways, and must deliver ready-to-hang work (D-rings and wire, Plexiglas not glass) to the gallery by February 5, 2027. The organiser's own entry page gives the deadline as November 9 while its CaFÉ listing states entries close at midnight Central on November 8 — the earlier of the two is stored here. That entry page also still prints a link to the retired 2024 CaFÉ listing, which now loads an empty page; the live listing is the one linked here. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–5 images), $60 (up to 10 images). Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: BLUE Photography Exhibit · Decode Gallery
item.description: Decode Gallery's juried exhibition on the colour blue, in every hue and shade — landscapes and seascapes, portraits and abstracts, and whatever the gallery calls the calm or melancholy the colour stirs up. The call is open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional alike, and there is no restriction on genre or process. At least 26 images are selected by juror Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer who founded Decode after a BA in Photography from the Art Institute of Seattle. Selected photographers pay nothing further: the gallery handles all printing itself on an Epson printer with Ilford Pearl paper and presents work in museum-quality 22 x 22 inch white frames with precut white mats (11 x 11, 10 x 15, 11 x 15, 12 x 15 inches and others), scaling files for the best fit in the mat without ever cropping them. One exhibition print is made per image and archived in a flat file for six months after the show. Entry is $40 for up to five photographs or $45 for up to ten. Photographers are notified by email within two weeks of the deadline, and high-resolution files are due two days after the acceptance email. The exhibition runs January 2 to January 30 at the gallery in Tucson, opening January 2. Work may optionally be listed for sale, with Decode taking a 50 per cent commission; all rights to the image file and the print remain with the photographer. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images, $45/10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SQUARE Photography Exhibit 2027 · Decode Gallery
item.description: The next edition of Decode Gallery's square-format show, challenging photographers to compose within the confines of the perfect square — from analog Hasselblads to digital Instagram feeds, the most persistent format in photography, where symmetry, balance, focus and narrative are all transformed by equal sides. Submissions are welcome from every photographic genre, including portraiture, landscape, documentary, architecture and conceptual work; the call is open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional alike. Twelve images are selected by juror Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer who founded Decode after a BA in Photography from the Art Institute of Seattle, and hang for an unusually long three months — February 6 to April 24, 2027 — at the gallery in Tucson, opening February 6. Selected photographers pay nothing further: the gallery handles all printing itself on an Epson printer with Ilford Pearl paper and presents work in museum-quality 14 x 14 inch frames with mats cut to 7 x 7 inches. One print is made per accepted image file and archived in a flat file for six months after the show. Entry is a flat $40 per entry, which the gallery's guidelines describe as covering up to ten photographs; the live entry form itself accepts fifteen files before it refuses more, so the ten is the entitlement the gallery states rather than a limit the form imposes. Photographers are notified by email within two weeks of the deadline. Work may optionally be listed for sale, with Decode taking a 50 per cent commission; all rights to the image file and the print remain with the photographer. The gallery states plainly that a paid entry does not guarantee a place in any exhibition. — Deadline: January 7, 2027. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: As Above, So Below — SaveArtSpace Bus Shelter Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on bus shelter advertising space in Miami during Miami Art Week, curated by the illustrator and muralist Marlon Pruz and opening November 27, 2026. As Above, So Below explores the idea that the patterns of the universe are reflected within us and that the inner world is inseparable from the outer one, considering the relationship between the cosmic and the earthly, the microscopic and the infinite — the way electrons orbiting an atomic nucleus mimic planets orbiting the sun, and the way the golden ratio and other recurring patterns in nature suggest an underlying order connecting all forms of life. Pruz says he is looking for work that creates a strong visual or conceptual dialogue between these realms: imagery connecting the body to nature, humanity to the cosmos, consciousness to environment, and the intimate to the infinite. The entry form gives the theme more plainly as Visionary Art and states that all art will be accepted. Open to artists of any age, skill level or background; corporate logos, personal advertising and video are excluded and still JPEGs only are accepted, so photographic work is eligible. Up to ten images may be uploaded at a maximum of 2 MB each, with high-resolution files requested from selected artists; the potential ad panel is 69 inches high by 48 inches wide, though the artwork itself can be any size. Submissions run September 23 to October 19, 2026 at 11:59pm, selected artists are announced after November 2, and the work goes up on Miami ad space from November 27 for at least one month. SaveArtSpace is a 501(c)(3) non-profit that has placed artists' work on commercial ad space since 2015; fees are tax-deductible donations that pay for the ad space, and every exhibition is curated, so applying does not guarantee installation. The entry form charges the stated donation plus card fees, so the amount actually taken at checkout is $36.92 for one to three images, rising to $108.45 for ten. — Deadline: October 19, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Bus shelter exhibition in Miami.

item.title: Empty Places : Abandoned Spaces · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: International juried photography exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on emptiness, absence and abandonment. The gallery's framing distinguishes the two: an empty place is not necessarily abandoned, and an abandoned space is rarely without evidence — one is defined by absence, the other by what remains, and both invite the same questions: who was here, what happened, why does the place continue to hold our attention. Praxis is looking for work on the visual and emotional weight of emptiness, from derelict factories and rural ruins to neglected homes, civic structures, vacant interiors and landscapes emptied of human presence, whether it documents decay or transforms emptiness into something poetic, symbolic, uncanny or surreal; the entry portal adds that all lens-based art is welcome. Up to 74 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (21 November – 12 December 2026), featured on the gallery's online exhibition page and permanently archived there. Awards are a Juror's Choice (free entry into three future juried calls of the artist's choice), a Directors' Choice (two future calls) and eight honourable mentions featured in the exhibition, the printed exhibition catalogue and the online gallery — there is no cash prize. Entrants must be 18 or older, and images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5, and artists experiencing financial hardship may request a free submission. Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's optional $37 printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing in its 22 × 22-inch black frames (mat openings up to 11 × 11, 10 × 15, 11.8 × 15 or 8 × 15 inches) and retains a 50% commission on any print sales. Notification is 30 October 2026. No juror is named for this call on either the gallery's own page or the entry portal, unlike its sibling call on the same page. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: Roadside Attractions: Art and History on Route 66
item.description: Gallery Seven and the Gaylord Building Historic Site are mounting this juried show together for Route 66's centennial, pairing an art component curated by the gallery with a history component built by the Gaylord Building, and it runs long — 12 November 2026 to 24 March 2027 in the Third Floor Founders' Gallery of the Gaylord Building in Lockport, Illinois, a National Trust site on the old highway itself. The brief is the legacy of Route 66 in Illinois and beyond, read both as a real transportation corridor and as a symbol of travel, community, roadside culture and American imagination. Photography is in: the prospectus states that all media is eligible except film/video, oversized works and special installations, and Gallery Seven has run Open Lens, its own community photography exhibition, every year since 2010. Open to any artist 18 or over with no geographic bar — the gallery accepts shipped work as well as drop-off, and will advise on shipping on request. One $50 fee covers up to five entries, with an extra image allowed free for each 3D piece. Awards total $800 in cash: Best of Show $250, 1st $175, 2nd $125, 3rd $100 and three Honorable Mentions of $50, presented at a 6–7pm ceremony on 10 March 2027; the gallery's own web page also names a People's Choice Award voted by visitors. Work must be original, never previously submitted to or shown at Gallery Seven, framed with hanging wire and bumpers, and no taller than 48 inches or wider than 36 including the frame. Everything must be for sale at the artist's own price with a 30% commission to the gallery, paid out within 45 days of closing; sold work stays on the wall to the end. Entries go by email as .jpg attachments at 72 DPI and 3000 pixels on the long side, with the entry form, and the fee is paid by PayPal on the gallery's site, by cheque or in person — note the two closing dates: email entries are accepted to 24 October 2026, but if you post a CD with the form instead it must be postmarked by 17 October. Selections are notified 28–29 October and delivered 5–7 November. The prospectus says entries are juried by independent jurors to be announced, while the gallery's own web page says the show will be juried and judged by the artist partners of Gallery Seven; no name is published either way. Anything left at the gallery after 24 March 2027 becomes its property. — Deadline: October 24, 2026. Fee: $50 for up to 5 works. Prize: $250 Best of Show + $175 1st + $125 2nd + $100 3rd + 3 × $50 Honorable Mention.

item.title: 2027 REAF Regional Erotic Art Show and Sale · Rochester Erotic Arts Festival
item.description: The juried art show at the heart of the Rochester Erotic Arts Festival, an adults-only weekend of art, performance, workshops and vending that moves to Ithaca for 2027 after losing its Auburn hotel. REAF is looking for high-quality original work that is "creative, erotic and thought-provoking", and photography is not a tolerated extra here — it is named in the accepted-media list alongside drawing, painting, printmaking, mixed media, collage, digital art, film and sculpture, and it has its own top award: Best in Photography, $100, matched by Best in Fine Art at $100 and three Producers Choice Awards of $50. Accepted artists get a free weekend Artist Pass to the whole festival and can buy a plus-one pass for $30. Work is offered for sale and REAF takes no commission — artists supply their own buyer contact details, which are displayed with the work, and deal with buyers directly. One entry is $30 and covers up to five pieces; an artist may file up to three entries, so fifteen pieces is the practical ceiling at $90. Work must not have been shown at REAF before. THIS IS A HAND-DELIVERY SHOW AND THAT IS THE REAL GATE: accepted work has to be brought in person to Ithaca, New York on the evening of Thursday 8 April or the morning of Friday 9 April 2027, ready to hang — matted, framed, signed and labelled — and cannot be collected before the exhibition closes; there is no shipping option, and the organiser describes the show as regional without naming a region. Prints other than photographs must be limited editions on archival paper, numbered and signed. Artists must be 18 or over, must hold a model release for any identifiable person photographed, and where a model is nude or in sexual activity must hold a legible copy of ID proving they were 18+; work depicting minors is refused outright. REAF carries no insurance on displayed work and recommends artists check their own. Submissions are open now; the deadline is 1 February 2027, decisions go out by 8 February, and accepted artists must respond by 15 February. The festival itself runs 9–11 April 2027 across the Ithaca Downtown Conference Center and The Hotel Ithaca, with ASL interpreters available all weekend. — Deadline: February 1, 2027. Fee: $30 per entry of up to 5 works. Prize: $100 Best in Photography + $100 Best in Fine Art + 3 × $50 Producers Choice.
